fields.name: Navakiśora Gosvāmīpāda
fields.disappearance: At Purī, during the Pāṇḍu-vijaya of the Ratha-yātrā; samādhi by Narendra-sarovara (the record's text)
fields.place: East Bengal; Vṛndāvana / Govardhana; Purī (samādhi by Narendra-sarovara)
fields.guru: Kṛṣṇakiśora, eldest son of Lakṣmīkānta Gosvāmī (dīkṣā); Siddha Kṛṣṇadāsa Bābā of Govardhana (who taught them bhajana)
fields.notes: Of the family of Lakṣmīkānta Gosvāmī, a scion of a disciple of Nityānanda; disciple of Kṛṣṇakiśora and guru and inseparable friend of Locanānanda (#1846). Posing as low-caste Hāḍis they served Siddha Kṛṣṇadāsa Bābā of Govardhana, who taught them bhajana; they preached in East Bengal and died together at Purī during the Ratha-yātrā; samādhi by Narendra-sarovara.

A descendant of Madhu Paṇḍita (#874). Ashamed when a disciple's wife asked him to speak about Kṛṣṇa, he gave up family life, lived at the Gopīnātha temple of Vṛndāvana as its accountant, read the Caitanya-caritāmṛta to the people and spent all he had on poor and sick Vaiṣṇavas; never let anyone take his foot-dust or remnants.

Of the Guhā family (Saptagrāma, Gauḍa); father of King Basanta Rāya of Jessore, uncle of Mahārāja Pratāpāditya. Settled in Vṛndāvana and about 1570 built the temple of Madana-mohana south of Kṛṣṇadāsa Kapūra's (inscription read by Growse); there Madana-gopāla, with the Rādhā and Lalitā sent by Puruṣottama Jānā, became «Madana-mohana». The Deity later went to Jaipur and Karauli; Gaura-Nitāi are now worshipped in his temple.
